title: Patch: a pull request that changes only a bot workflow runs the web test that reads every workflow, and the scope test checks each file of a directory a source reads
thread:
**Issue #5002 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #5002: Patch: a pull request that changes only a bot workflow runs the web test that reads every workflow, and the scope test checks each file of a directory a source reads
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

CI skips almost every job for a pull request that changes only files no test reads, such as the bots' own workflow files. But one of the web's tests does read every workflow file. It checks that only two workflows may use production's statistics database login, that only one may import statistics, and that no retired training lane comes back. Today, a pull request that edits only one of seven bot workflows skips that test, and so does the merge queue. A broken rule shows up only after the pull request lands, as a red run on main.

Once this is built, such a pull request runs the web job. The test that keeps the skip list honest also checks each file of a directory a test reads, so this kind of gap fails CI. Whoever edits those seven workflows notices, because their pull requests run a few more minutes of CI.

## Why

- **The test reads every workflow.** `apps/web/src/net/env-production.test.ts:135-137` reads every `.github/workflows/*.yml` (`readdirSync(WORKFLOWS)`). Three ruling tests assert over all of them:
  - R4701000 (`:149-158`): no workflow names a retired learn or self-play lane or its scripts.
  - R1933001 (`:160-179`): only `gather.yml` runs `stats-import`.
  - R1933000 (`:181-187`): only `db-size.yml` and `winrates-refresh.yml` name `STATS_DATABASE_URL`, production's statistics login.
- **Seven of them are on the skip list.** `scripts/ci-scope.sh:240-243` lists `bot-commands.yml`, `bot-night.yml`, `squishy-run.yml`, `squishy-commands.yml`, `triage.yml`, `ci-duration.yml` and `pr-title.yml`. A diff of only those prints `full=false`, so `web (unit k/K)` is skipped.
- **That breaks the script's own header.** Line 59 says "Nothing a test, a build or a check reads is on the list". The test's workflow scan and these seven skip-list entries both arrived in #2758 (2026-11-02), so the header has been wrong since then.
- **What could slip through.** A pull request that adds `STATS_DATABASE_URL` to `bot-night.yml` would hand the bots' runs production's statistics login, and R1933000 would run on neither the pull request nor its merge-queue build. The push to main runs what the queue skipped (`ci.yml:79-80`), so the break first appears as a red main after the merge. Every later merge-queue run that runs `web` then fails on it too, whatever that pull request changed.
- **The check meant to catch this cannot see it.** `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` collects every path the web's sources name and asserts that ci-scope runs `web` for it (`:861-870`). But `named()` (`:793-799`) turns a named directory into `${path}/x`. So it asks about `.github/workflows/x`, which is not skip-listed and runs everything, and never about the seven files. Its pins at `:144-145` and `:155` even hold those seven to running nothing.
- **What it costs.** In the last month 13 commits touched these seven workflows, and only 2 of them touched nothing else (`1c6a763abc`, `9230e2fad6`, both `ci-duration.yml`). So about two pull requests a month would run `full`'s baseline (the release build, the checks, fuzz 200, the classifier) plus `web`, not every job.

## Proposal

1. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, take the seven workflows off `skipped()` and give them a case of their own, ahead of the `.github/*` run-everything case, that turns on `web` alone, the one job that reads them. Correct the header's skip-list paragraph to match.
2. In `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, change the pins at `:144-145` and `:155` to expect `web` on for each of the seven.
3. Make the source scan check a named directory file by file for every tracked file under it that the skip list names, keeping today's `${path}/x` probe for the directory itself. A test that lists a directory is then held to each skip-listed file in it.

## Where it lands

- `scripts/ci-scope.sh`
- `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`
- Nothing under `.github/`, and no test under `bot/` pins these seven paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A diff of only `.github/workflows/bot-night.yml`, run through `scripts/ci-scope.sh` the way `ci-scope.test.ts`'s throwaway repositories run it, gives `full=true` and `web=true`, with `e2e`, `clippy`, the db suites and every `rust_*` group false.
- [ ] The same holds for each of the other six workflows.
- [ ] With the seven put back on the skip list, the new directory check in `ci-scope.test.ts` fails, naming `apps/web/src/net/env-production.test.ts` and each workflow.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/env-production.test.ts` pass.

## Size and risks

- **Size:** small, one case in a shell script and its test, difficulty medium.
- **Cost:** a pull request that touches only those workflows runs a few minutes more CI.
- **Risk:** expanding named directories could multiply the scan's test cases if a source names a large directory. Limiting the expansion to files the skip list names keeps it to these seven today.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Area: `tests` (`suggestions.areas`).

Class: `checks` → `priority:low`; relabel to change it.

**Judge:** leaves it to a person: The gap is real (the seven skip-listed workflows skip the web test that scans every workflow), but no break is cited, it adds CI to pull requests the pins keep cheap on purpose, and ci.yml's header accepts that a scoping mistake turns up on the push to main, so whether it's worth it is a maintainer's call.
```
